description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Buccaneers beat reporter Scott Reynolds suggested the team may want to reduce Bucky Irving's workload to allow him to be more effective this season.
items.impact: Reynolds notes that there's a reason why Bucs head coach Todd Bowles has called Irving and Kenneth Gainwell 1A and 1B. The Bucs gave Gainwell a two-year, $14 million deal in free agency and he has reportedly impressed new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson. Gainwell emerged in a big way with the Steelers last season and it appears he could be in line for another similar role in the backfield for Tampa Bay. Irving is expected to be good to go in training camp, but he missed time earlier in the teams offseason program recovering from a shoulder injury.
items.title: Bucky Irving could see reduced workload to be more effective

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Patriots waive WR Jimmy Kibble with an injury designation.
items.impact: Kibble signed as an unrestricted free agent in May. He will figure to seek another opportunity.
items.title: Jimmy Kibble waived by Patriots

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: The Ravens are signing wide receiver Chris Moore.
items.impact: Moore reunites with the Ravens, who drafted him in the fourth round in 2016 before he played five seasons with the team. He appeared in 14 games for the Commanders last season, making 11 catches for 207 yards and a touchdown.
items.title: Chris Moore signing with Ravens

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Titans signed Nazeeh Johnson.
items.impact: Johnson played only two games last season after injuring a shoulder in the preseason. He will compete for a depth role in the Titans secondary.
items.title: Nazeeh Johnson signs with Titans

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Seahawks signed TE Nick Vannett.
items.impact: Vannett earns a spot in training camp with the Seahawks following a tryout. He was drafted by Seattle back in 2016.
items.title: Nick Vannett signs with Seahawks

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Ravens hosted WR Dante Pettis for a tryout on Friday.
items.impact: Pettis caught 19 passes with the Bears last season. He will compete for a spot in training camp with Baltimore.
items.title: Dante Pettis works out for Ravens

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Ravens hosted WR Sterling Shepard for a tryout on Friday.
items.impact: Shepard caught 34 passes with the Bucs last season. He will compete for a spot in training camp with Baltimore.
items.title: Sterling Shepard works out for Ravens

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: The Panthers have claimed offensive lineman Ryan Hayes off waivers from the Titans.
items.impact: Hayes was recently waived by Tennessee, but will land with the Panthers in the early stages of training camp. The 26-year-old has just one career NFL regular-season game on his resume from the 2024 season while with the Dolphins.
items.title: Ryan Hayes claimed by Panthers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Panthers signed DT Kyon Barrs.
items.impact: Barrs had a successful workout with Carolina. He'll add depth on its offensive line.
items.title: Kyon Barrs signs with Panthers

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: The Panthers have waived wide receiver Kobe Prentice.
items.impact: The Panthers signed Prentice as an undrafted free agent, but he has been waived to make room for offensive lineman Ryan Hayes, who the team claimed off waivers from the Titans on Friday.
items.title: Kobe Prentice waived by Panthers

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: Chiefs defensive lineman Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) will likely begin training camp on the physically unable to perform list.
items.impact: Norman-Lott sustained a season-ending right ACL tear in a win over the Raiders in Week 7 last season. The 24-year-old will begin his second training camp on the PUP list, but it's unclear how long he will be out as players are eligible to come off the PUP list at any point during camp.
items.title: Omar Norman-Lott (knee) to begin camp on PUP list

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: Chiefs wideout Rashee Rice (knee) is 'doing great' and is 'cleared to go', according to head coach Andy Reid.
items.impact: Rice has been rehabbing his right knee this off-season after undergoing a cleanup procedure. The talented receiver also did a 30-day stint in jail after violating the terms of his probation this spring. Rice should once again form a quality duo with Patrick Mahomes, who was also cleared to practice following last season's ACL injury.
items.title: Rashee Rice (knee) 'doing great', cleared to go

items.author: Brenton Kemp
items.desc: Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee) has been cleared to participate in practice, according to head coach Andy Reid.
items.impact: Reid informed the media that Mahomes has been cleared to practice to begin training camp after suffering a torn ACL last season. The two-time MVP certainly appears on track to start Week 1 against a tough Denver Broncos defense.
items.title: Patrick Mahomes (knee) cleared to practice

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: The Steelers officially signed Drew Allar to his rookie contract.
items.impact: Allar lands his deal heading into training camp. He will be competing for the backup job behind Aaron Rodgers in the Steelers quarterback room.
items.title: Drew Allar signs rookie contract with Steelers
